title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Routine follow-up for management of type 2 diabetes and peripheral neuropathy.

HPI
The patient reports generally feeling well since the last visit. They continue to manage their type 2 diabetes mellitus with prescribed medications. They are aware of their peripheral neuropathy and report no new changes in numbness or tingling since the last evaluation. They continue to take both their insulin and metformin as directed.

Medication List
Insulin (specific type omitted), Metformin

Exam
Vitals are stable. Neurological exam reveals decreased sensation in a stocking distribution consistent with known peripheral neuropathy. Cardiovascular and pulmonary exams are unremarkable.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Stable on current regimen.
2. Peripheral neuropathy: Status post evaluation.

Plan
Continue current regimen of insulin and metformin for type 2 diabetes mellitus. Follow up as scheduled for routine monitoring of peripheral neuropathy. Patient educated on adherence to medication schedule.
explanations: Polyneuropathy is listed under 'with' for diabetes: the combination code E11.42 captures both.
When both insulin and oral hypoglycemics are used, assign both Z79.4 and Z79.84.

distractors.why: Coding the two separately misses the presumed link.
Both Z codes are assigned when both drug types are used.
